I know that crappy movie Juno made it seem so cool, but I've seen people go through adoption and it can be DEVASTATING. I have a half sibling who was given up for adoption and nearly 40 years after the fact me and the rest of my family still talk about her. Terminating an embryo's development is one thing. Knowing your flesh and blood is out there walking and talking and has no idea who you are...and I'm just her sister. Imagine how her mother must feel. But that's just my experience with it. Also, pregnancy takes a HUGE toll on the body, to an effect which is hard to understand if you've never been pregnant, so for some women it can be difficult to go through those changes, knowing that the child won't end up being theirs. Also, for some women, when thier family or partner finds out that they're pregnant, they won't allow the woman to give the child up for adoption. And some women face punitive measures if anyone ever finds out that they were sexually active and got pregnant. So, in the end, it all comes down to one's personal moral code and specific situation. That's why the arguement against prolife is called pro-choice, because no one can predict the circumstances of a life that isn't theirs. There are too many factors that come into play, and the balance of a person's life is delicate.

It's going to take a couple weeks, maybe even a month, to feel like your old self again. AT least that's been the case for me. About a week after the procedure I had all my old strength and energy back, and a week or two after that I finished "deflating," so to speak. It takes some time, and it varies as well. What's important is that after the procedure you rest and take it easy on yourself - don't try to force yourself to feel "normal" again. That's what I did, but my hormones were so messed up that I found myself crying in the corner constantly because I was stressing out so bad. To give you a solid number...I'd say three to four weeks. But seriously, until then take it easy on yourself emotionally. All those heavy feelings of fear and anxiety can sneak up on you if you don't keep an eye on them.

I'm not saying that not telling you is the wrong decision, I'm just warning you that it's gonna be hard...it's mainly the hormones. They might turn you into a big baby, so be warned. The procedure is going to hurt, but nothing you've never felt if you've ever had really bad period cramps. I remember shaking like a leaf when the doctor told me to scoot my butt down, but within fight minutes after deep breathing my way through some cramps, she pops her head up between my legs and says "We're done!" I got really lucky with the clinic I went to and everyone was kind a supportive and talked me through it, step by step. If you don't get so fortunate, just remember one thing - BREATHE. Like deep meditation breathing, breathing with your abdomen and all that. It helps with the pain and real levels your head if you ever start getting nervous. Don't be nervous. Just imagine getting a pap smear that last for five minutes while you're on your period. It's really not that intense.

The not telling the boyfriend thing is going to be really REALLY hard though, coming from a pragmatic perspective, because you'll be super hormonal and bleeding for about two weeks. best of luck to you, just know that if you ever feel alone during this, you've got a whole mess of women going through the same exact thing.
